trials.output_text: {"subjective": "Patient reports headaches almost every evening for three weeks. Headaches are at the back of the head and sometimes across the forehead, described as heavy and pressing. Paracetamol helps a little. Headaches are worse when stressed or skipping lunch. No vomiting, blurred vision, flashing lights, or weakness. Patient has occasional blurry vision in the evening that clears. No fever or stiff neck. Patient has been taking amlodipine five milligrams once daily, but misses it sometimes. Patient has been taking metformin five hundred milligrams twice daily with meals, but often forgets the evening dose. Patient checks blood pressure at home and reports readings of one fifty over ninety and one forty-eight over ninety-two. Patient has a glucometer and reports morning blood sugar around nine to ten, and after meals around twelve. Patient wakes up two times per night to urinate and is thirsty. Patient has lost about two or three kilograms in the last two months. Patient experiences tingling in both feet, mostly at night, getting worse. Patient has no sores on his feet. No chest pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath. Patient reports mild ankle swelling in the evening. Patient drinks one to two sodas daily. Patient likes salty food. Patient stopped smoking four years ago and drinks two or three beers on Saturdays. Patient does not exercise regularly. Patient's father had diabetes and died of a stroke at sixty-three. His mother has high blood pressure. His brother has diabetes. Patient reports mood is okay, but sleep is poor (five hours). Patient is worried about health and work.
